handbookNote: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific sections revised 12/2024), published by Kentucky State Police (KSP) / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- fetched from the Kentucky State Police-hosted copy at https://wp.kentuckystatepolice.ky.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2025-CDL-Manual-in-PDF-Format-V1.pdf on 2026-08-22 (5.85MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext to scratchpad/ky_cdl_research/ky_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,850 lines); the drive.ky.gov-hosted copy of the same manual (https://drive.ky.gov/Drivers/Documents/2025-CDL-Manual-6-4-2025.pdf) returned an HTTP error at fetch time, so the Kentucky State Police mirror was used instead -- both are official Kentucky Commonwealth (.ky.gov) sources and Kentucky State Police is the agency that actually administers CDL knowledge and skills testing in Kentucky. Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics, confirmed directly from the official Kentucky-specific front matter of this manual (unlike several other CDL-track states in this project, e.g. Indiana, where no official source states an exact item count): the General Knowledge test consists of 50 questions covering vehicle operations, cargo handling, and vehicle inspection; applicants for a Class A license face an additional 20-question Combination Vehicles test; applicants driving air-brake-equipped vehicles face an additional 25-question Air Brakes test; endorsement tests are 20 questions each for Doubles/Triples, Tankers, and Passenger Transport, 30 questions for Hazardous Materials, and 20 questions for School Bus. For every test, 80 percent of questions must be answered correctly to pass (also the federally standardized minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a)). Kentucky's six CDL endorsement codes are H (Hazardous Materials), N (Tank), P (Passenger), T (Double/Triple Trailer), X (Tank/Hazardous Materials combined), and S (School Bus) -- notably Kentucky does NOT use a separate 'C' charter-bus endorsement. Kentucky's restriction-code table (L, Z, E, O, M, N, K, V, P, X, and '8' for other special restrictions) is unusually granular; a CDL instruction permit is valid for six months, must be held at least 14 days before the CDL skills test may be attempted, and may only be renewed once; the general-knowledge test may be retaken indefinitely with only a 24-hour wait and no fee, while the combination/air-brake/endorsement tests carry a $5 retest fee after the initial failure; the Hazardous Materials endorsement requires FBI/TSA fingerprint-based background checks and must be retested at every CDL renewal; School Bus endorsement requires the applicant to also hold a Passenger endorsement and pass a knowledge test on manual Sections 2, 4, and 10. Content-depth rationale: Kentucky uses the same AAMVA-authored 'Modernized Testing System' base manual (Version: September 9, 2022) as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Indiana), organized into the same 13 sections -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into two buckets for volume), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split here into two buckets), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving -- plus Kentucky-specific administrative detail (testing structure, permit rules, retesting, endorsements/restrictions, disqualifications, medical waivers, farm-related-services restricted CDL, 18-20-year-old intrastate provision) layered into the licensing bucket from the manual's Kentucky-specific front matter (pages 1-9). Some sections (Cargo, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Kentucky manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
